name: Diffusion Policy (CNN, real-world setting)
family: Imitation policy: ResNet-18 encoders, 1D temporal U-Net, DDIM

sources.title: C. Chi et al., Diffusion Policy: Visuomotor Policy Learning via Action Diffusion, arXiv:2303.04137
sources.covers: Table 7 image and crop resolutions and horizons, Appendix A.3 cropping, Appendix D cameras and down-sampling, the inference latency, the 10 Hz command rate

note: The figures are the paper's real-world tasks with the CNN-based policy (Table 7): camera video down-sampled to 320 × 240, then a 288 × 216 crop, random in training and "a static center crop with the same size" at inference. How a 16:9 720p stream becomes 320 × 240 is not stated (stretched or cropped); DexVantage applies pre_resize as a stretch, an assumption. It is not a ViT (a ResNet-18 with spatial softmax pooling), so patch_px and tokens_per_image are null. Simulation tasks use other sizes (for example 96 × 96 cropped to 84 × 84 for Push-T): override input_resolution and pre_resize for them. To 2 observation steps; Tp 16 predicted, Ta 8 executed. Commands at 10 Hz are linearly interpolated to 125 Hz. The 0.1 s inference time is Section 3.4's figure for DDIM with 10 inference iterations on an Nvidia 3080; Table 7 lists 16 evaluation iterations (D-Iters Eval) for the real-world tasks, so the timing is for a lighter setting than the table's and may understate it (truthfulness review 2026-11-07, paper read again).

crop_rule.quote: "we employed random crop augmentation during training"; "During inference, we take a static center crop with the same size." (Appendix A.3)

pre_resize.quote: UR5 station: 720p RGB video "down-sampled to 320x240 at 10fps"; Franka station: VGA images "downsampled to 320x240 at 10fps" (Appendix D)

patch_px.quote: Not a ViT: "We used a standard ResNet-18 (without pretraining) as the encoder" with spatial softmax pooling.

n_cameras.quote: UR5 station: "Only 2 of the cameras are used for policy observation"; the Franka station "has 2 realsense D415"

action_chunk.quote: Table 7: Tp (action prediction horizon) 16 for the real-world tasks

execute_steps.quote: Table 7: Ta 8 for Pour, Spread and Mug Flip (6 for real Push-T); "the action horizon of 8 steps to be optimal for most tasks that we tested"

temporal_ensemble_m.quote: Not stated: the paper uses receding-horizon control.

inference_ms.quote: "enables 0.1s inference latency on a Nvidia 3080 GPU" (DDIM, 100 training and 10 inference iterations)

control_hz.quote: "Diffusion Policy predicts robot commands at 10 Hz" (linearly interpolated to 125 Hz)
